newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine gov't hopes to restart union talks.
newsitem.headline: Argentine gov't hopes to restart union talks.

text.p: Argentina's cabinet chief Jorge Rodriguez said Tuesday he has had initial talks with members of the main CGT union federation to "restart the dialogue" after last week's general strike.

"I had a brief meeting this morning with some leaders of the CGT to see if there is a chance of continuing the dialogue, and I think there is a lot of goodwill," Rodriguez said in comments reported by state news agency Telam.
The CGT staged a 24-hour general strike on Dec 26 -- the third this year -- protesting at government plans to reform labor legislation, seen by unions as reducing their powers.

The strike was called as President Carlo Menem signed three decrees on labor reforms after talks with the unions broke down. Menem believes labor reforms are crucial to its efforts to reduce the 17.3 percent unemployment rate.
Rodriguez said he hoped talks between the government, business leaders and the unions could restart but added: "They will not be easy negotiations."
